summary: Pavel Poucha specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Charles University (1924–1929) under Vincenc Lesný and Oldřich Hujer, later serving as a docent at the Oriental Institute (1948–1958).

Linguist Pavel Trost earned his PhD at Charles University under Friedrich Karl Slotty (1934) and completed his PD at Palacký University Olomouc. He held posts at Masaryk University, Palacký University, and Charles University (docent 1956–1975).
Working in Indology and philosophy, Pavle Jevtić was a disciple of Dimitrije Mitrinović and earned a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London (~1923–1927).

Pavlo Grigorovič Ritter was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Kharkiv under Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij and under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He became a professor at the University of Kharkiv in 1921, succeeding Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij.

Working in linguistics and Indology, Pawan Goyal earned an M.Tech. from IIT Madras and a Ph.D. from the Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems. He is attested at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (2018–2025).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology, Pe Maung Tin studied at the universities of Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as professor of Pali and principal at the University of Rangoon and chairman of the Burma Historical Commission.
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

Pedro Roca y López worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Juan Gelabert y Gordiola, earned a Dr.phil. from Complutense University of Madrid, and held posts as librarian at the University of Barcelona and the National Library of Spain.

id: P:Pedro Urbano González de la Calle
summary: Pedro Urbano González de la Calle worked in Indology and linguistics, completing his Ph.D. at Complutense University of Madrid. He held professorships and posts at the universities of Salamanca, Valencia, Madrid, Barcelona, Bogotá, UNAM, and El Colegio de México.
Pei-jung Wu, working in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology, earned a B.A. from National Taiwan University and a Ph.D. from UCLA (completed 2002) under Donald F. McCallum.

Tibetologist Pema Bhum was formerly a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and served as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Buddhist studies scholar Pema Chödrön studied at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley. A disciple of Chögyam Trungpa, among other teachers, she has served as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center and as director and abbess of Gampo Abbey.
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Pema Donyo Nyinje studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Pema Gyaltsen studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, and taught Christopher S. George, Adam Pearcey, and Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Pema Sherpa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, attested in 2026 as a PhD candidate in Religious Studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Tibetologist Pema Tsering studied under Shenphen Nangwa and served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn (attested 1982).
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
